english.notes:
(i) Proceedings for an offence under this Act may be brought within the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the prosecutor to warrant the proceedings came to his knowledge (section 9(3)), but subsection (3) does not authorise the commencement of proceedings for an offence more than 2 years after the date on which the offence was committed (section 9(4) Deer Act 1991).
(ii) A certificate signed by the or on behalf of the prosecutor and stating the date on which evidence sufficient in his opinion to warrant the proceedings came to his knowledge shall be conclusive evidence of that fact (section 9(5)). A certificate stating that matter and purporting to be so signed shall be deemed to be so signed unless the contrary is proved (section 9(6)).
(iii) Section 12(1) of the Deer Act 1991 provides for stop and search powers.
(iv) Section 12(2) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that for the purposes of-
(a) exercising the powers conferred under subsection (1) above, or
(b) arresting a person, in accordance with section 24 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (arrest conditions), for an offence under this Act, a constable may enter any land other than a dwelling-house.
(v) Section 13(1) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that the court by which a person is convicted of any offence under this Act may order the forfeiture of-
(a) any deer or venison in respect of which the offence was committed or which was found in that person's possession;
(b) any vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing which was used to commit the offence or which was capable of being used to take, kill, or injure deer and was found in his possession.
(vi) Section 13(2) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that where the offence of which the person is convicted is an offence under section 1, the court (without prejudice to its powers under subsection (1) above) may cancel any firearm or shotgun certificate held by him.
